sections.content: How many people stayed in Ackworth Moor Top after gaining qualifications?

Ackworth Moor Top is a small town in Yorkshire and The Humber. Ackworth Moor Top does not have its own university.

Ackworth Moor Top has lower levels of deprivation.

Overall, Ackworth Moor Top ended up with:

  • more graduates than it produced
  • more non-graduates with advanced qualifications than it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 205 state-school pupils from Ackworth Moor Top who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 65 (32%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 60 (29%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Ackworth Moor Top to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Ackworth Moor Top's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Ackworth Moor Top in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

In 2018 to 2019, 58% of graduates and 50% of qualified non-graduates living in Ackworth Moor Top had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 95 graduates and 80 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Ackworth Moor Top. This is compared with the 65 graduates and 60 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 42% of the graduates had also lived in Ackworth Moor Top as GCSE pupils, while 58% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Ackworth Moor Top in 2018 to 2019, 50% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 50% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
